# s322 — Print a slice's orchestrator brief with ai relay-brief

`slicer ai relay-brief ID --worktree PATH --branch NAME --run RUN --step N` prints the slice-specific orchestrator brief, filled from the item, the role matrix, the finish step and a project template, so the outer session stops assembling briefs by hand.

**Findings:** outer-session wishlist 2026-10-16, item 1: hand-assembled briefs caused wrong commit titles and parallel names · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-16** — From the s320 relay (2026-10-16): build the brief's roles from roles.resolve and pass the accepted --prefer-agent/--select through, so the brief carries the accepted lineup, orchestrator included.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** spawning agents; recording the run (the outer session still runs `relay-run begin`/`step`); briefs for implementer, reviewer and gate roles (the orchestrator writes those); this repo's own environment lines, which the owner sets with `template set` after it lands.

## Why

In the v1.12 relays on 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-16 the outer session built every orchestrator brief by editing the previous one with Python and `sed`. Three errors reached the briefs:
- the s296 commit title stayed in the s298 and s307 briefs until a grep caught it;
- the s308 and s309 briefs named s298 as the slice running in parallel;
- a `RUN=` prefix was dropped.

Every slice-specific value is already known to slicer: id, title, size and effort, the role rows `relay-roles recommend` picks, `implement_finish` and `handoff_requires_note_kind`, the run and step ids. The project-specific environment lines (interpreter, TMPDIR rule, the `S()` helper) differ per project, so they belong in a template the project owns, like the render templates.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ai.py`: `relay_brief(state, item_id, *, worktree, branch, run, step, parallel, well_specified, split)` builds the brief from a template. The values:
  - id, title, size and effort;
  - the roles from the same code `relay-roles recommend` runs, with agent type, vendor, model and effort per role, and "no architect" unless the matrix picks one;
  - the finish override text: for `handoff`, `start` then `handoff` before review, `note` after PASS, never `done` in the worktree;
  - the end point, a commit titled `ID: TITLE`;
  - RUN and the orchestrator's step id;
  - the parallel slices from repeatable `--parallel ID`, with the files both touch (with the shared paths once "next --batch picks slices whose files do not overlap" has landed; until then just the ids).
- A new template `relay-brief.md` beside `slice.md`, `roadmap.md` and `row.md`, editable with `slicer template set relay-brief.md --stdin` and reset with `template reset`.
  - The built-in text has the contract pointer (`slicer ai relay-orchestrator`), the Rules the orchestrator needs (waiting, stop and report, single handback) and an empty ENVIRONMENT block.
  - Placeholders follow the existing template syntax.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: the `ai relay-brief` subcommand. `--json` returns `{"brief": text, "roles": [...], "contract": "relay v4"}`. An unknown id is `no_such_item`. An item with no slice, or with a required section empty, is `unspecified`.
- `docs/agents.md`, `docs/commands.md`, `docs/templates.md` (or wherever templates are documented), `CHANGELOG.md` under Added.
- `tests/test_ai.py`, `tests/test_templates.py`.
